text_fidelity_a:
Kelsyus Premium Floating Lounger XL with Fast Inflation, Inflatable Recliner Chair, Lake & Pool Float for Adults with Cup Holder, Amazon Exclusive First the good.
I shot light rapids in this puppy on the Blackfoot River in Montana. The collapsibility makes it easy to bring even if you don't have a pickup truck. You could put several in a compact car. You can blow it up with your own lungs in under five minutes, easily. It has good back support, very comfortable. The nylon cover protects from rocks. The foot rest and low profile give unparalleled maneuverability in rapids. You can get your arms deeper into the water than a traditional tube and the brace your feet on the foot rest to keep your seat when the ride gets wild. The handles allow you to stay in when it gets hectic. I got dumped once and because I was holding the handles, I was able to spin in a downhill rapid and shove it underwater and back under my tuchas to regain my seat.
It has all the advantages of an innertube and a kayak with the comfort of a recliner. The cup holder is also handy.
The bad:
The mesh is flimsy. All they need to do is use the stuff that more common blue and white float tubes use and they have a far better product. I got two small holes going over rocks. That doesn't happen with the blue and white tubes.
Fortunately, I can sew. I'm going to get some better mesh and pimp my floaty!
text_fidelity_b: Kelsyus Premium Floating Lounger XL with Fast Inflation, Inflatable Recliner Chair, Lake & Pool Float for Adults with Cup Holder, Amazon Exclusive

text_fidelity_a:
Lucky Ducks - The Memory and Matching Game That Moves - Includes A Fun Pop The Pig Make-A-Match Card Game The only bad thing about this game is the fact that my 2 year thinks it's a radio. We've had it for about a month now, and as I write this, it's "playing" in the background. It's playing in the background almost every night, if not during the day, too. It's super annoying! :P It's supposed to sound like ducks, I guess, but it's just lots of squeaking.

Otherwise, it's super cute, and my boys love playing it. I think 2-4 year old children will enjoy it the most, but it's labeled 3 and up. I imagine this is due to the stickers that must go on the ducks, and game board(which is a motorized pond). You do need batteries! There are 4 colors of stickers, 4 each. 3 of each will go on ducks and 1 on the game board. I wasn't paying attention enough to realize one of each color went on the game board. I ended up having to peel some stickers off of ducks.

You put the ducks on the game board, assign a color to each child(up to 4 players), and then press the center button. The ducks will then circle around the pond. Taking turns the child picks up a duck and turns it over. If it matches their assigned color, they keep it. If not, they put it back on the pond. While all the ducks are on the pond, it's a little crowded, so it was tough for my 2 year old to get the duck placed back on there without knocking over another duck, or several. It's easier to turn the pond off while your child is looking at the color and placing it back on the pond.

Overall, this is a fun game to teach a few colors, along with the art of taking turns and patience. My children had so much fun with it, they were impatient for their turn.
text_fidelity_b: Lucky Ducks - The Memory and Matching Game That Moves - Includes A Fun Pop The Pig Make-A-Match Card Game

Mattel Games UNO: Roboto Game I have to remember that we are living in a society that remakes or revamps everything....from movies (Planet of the Apes, Star Wars, Star Trek, etc) to television shows (Charlie's Angels), it was only a matter of time before they remade/revamped classic games that I grew up with (Uno, Monopoly, and Operation). And while I am still can't decide if that is a good thing or not, I do think that this version will appeal to most. While I can usually "trick" my 10 and 13 year old sons to play Classic Uno, I wondered would this version of the game appeal to them more because it has a computerized component. After all, the robot is cute with it's little voice, and the cards fit nicely in a holder on it's head. Especially because today's generation plays XBox, Nintendo, PSP, and the WII. I hoped that they would enjoy it especially on family night.

Surprisingly, this version was extremely interactive, entertaining and tons of fun....throwing out names and house rules, which provided a new twist to an already enjoyable game. The "new" additions to the Classic include: the ability to record the names of the players; the ability to add creative house rules where the last person to complete the task draws two cards; and the ability to add surprise commands. In other words, you can make this game as funny as you want.And while my kids initially thought it was lame, they have asked to play it several times creating silly rules and cute nicknames. I definitely think this game will appeal to some.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Games UNO: Roboto Game

text_fidelity_a:
Winning Moves Games Classic Twister Ah, the memories I have from playing Twister when I was 16 and drove a red Firebird. Paul, who I wished was my boyfriend was interested in me only as a friend, so the best way I had to get close to him was to invite friends over for a game of Twister. Memories are interesting because I recall exactly what he and I were both wearing -- he in a light blue oxford Gant shirt and me in my self designed and sewn striped wide legged hip-hugger slacks, solid shirt and matching striped vest. I can't tell you who else was there, but we had a full house and we had a blast with my little sister calling our moves and tattling when we were having TOO much fun.

[[ASIN:B00HVTH2MC Classic Twister]] can be played by most ages, provided the bodies are somewhat agile and the individuals are not really shy. The vinyl mat allows for between 2 and 4 people, no more. A game lasts less than 15 minutes usually with the winner being the person who remains on the mat without falling over. A designated person who is not on the mat spins the little plastic on cardboard wheel and those playing place the appropriate limb on a designated spot. For color blind people, your friends will let you know where to put that foot or hand, I guarantee. It is a really fun physical game that stimulates conversation and breaks the ice. I noticed that there are several versions of the game available as of today but cannot tell you what the differences are or why the prices vary. When I received this item I was a bit surprised at how large it is, bigger than I expected. I was thinking this would be approximately the size of a bread loaf pan (a testament to how terrible my sense of measure is), so when the box arrived I was surprised when I opened it to find this large plastic truck.

This truck is all plastic which has some pluses and minuses about it. It’s not all that expensive, which would not be the case if it was metal or had metal parts in it. It’s completely waterproof, and it is made well enough to handle some limited abuse. It is not made of heavy-grade plastic, though, so if it is thrown or stood upon it could break.

There are moving parts but everything is manual. No levers, no buttons, no wheels other than the tires, so play isn’t as automated. This may or may not frustrate a young child, though that depends on the child and not the toy. It’s not a toy for the impatient.

This is a decent toy though there are some trade-offs. For the price it is a good unit that will keep a patient child busy. It is not the sturdiest nor is it the most technologically advanced, so it can be broken if handled very roughly and it may prove frustrating for a child who expects some automation.

Educational Insights GeoSafari Fossil Excavation Kit, Kids Science Kit, Dinosaur Science Toy, Ages 7+ All of the fossils were in a single spot, and it took only a second to find them. I soaked the block in water, as I didn't want to take hours to dig them out, and after a little bit, I was able to pull the fossils out of the block with ease. I got this kit specifically for the trilobite, as I have always wanted one and didn't have one yet. So imagine my dismay when my new trilobite is crumbling to pieces in front of me. It couldn't have been damaged by my not digging correctly, as I didn't even dig at all.

I looked it over and I was upset to find spots that had been glued together. That tells me they knew it was coming apart when they included it. I guess they thought it was going to go to a kid who would just assume they broke it by being careless and would just throw it out and not care, but I personally don't like that they included a piece that was crumbling. There are other reviews that have the same problem with their trilobite crumbling and there are also others with pictures of the same.

The other fossils are all fine, and if you don't care at all about the trilobite, then I guess this kit is still ok to get. But I can't bring myself to recommend it to anyone because they knowingly included a broken and glued back together fossil.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights GeoSafari Fossil Excavation Kit, Kids Science Kit, Dinosaur Science Toy, Ages 7+

text_fidelity_a:
3Doodler Start Essentials 3D Pen Set For Kids with Free Refill Filament - STEM Toy For Boys & Girls, Age 6 & Up - Toy of The Year Award Winner I think this thing is awesome!

That said, I do have a couple of warnings to consider. First, it will get really expensive! The sticks don't go very far at all. (The package claims each 6 inch stick will give you 60 inches of play, so I'm going to assume we just need more practice to get that much, as I'm guessing most others will, too.) With this set, you'll get 2 packs of the sticks(48 total sticks...6 each of white, mint green, yellow, orange, blue, red, green, and grey). You'll use those up super quick! These sticks are biodegradable, BPA-free and labeled as "safe". From what I've read, you'll need these specific sticks to go with the 3Doodler.

Also, every time you put a new color stick through the pen, you'll be wasting a bit of the previous stick, unless it works into your design. The whole stick won't completely feed through until you put another one in there to push it on out.

It takes a great deal of practice to get anything worthwhile to turn out. I have 3 little boys and they all want a chance at practicing, so even more sticks are used up in that process. So far, we haven't came up with anything close to what is shown in the practice book, but none of us can call ourselves overly skilled in the artistic realm at this point in time.

All of that said, IF your budget allows for buying lots of sticks to go with this pen, it truly is awesome! (Or you could request packs of these sticks as grandparent presents for the kids.) ;) Letting a child use his/her imagination with this thing is an amazing opportunity, and I definitely recommend it. (I even recommend it for adults, too, because we all need a little childish fun every once in awhile!)

It's easy to use. Just charge it up with the included micro USB cable(or do like me and use your kindle charger), turn it on and wait for the light to turn green. Then, press the button to start it and press it again to stop it. Simple! As I mentioned earlier, there is a book with instructions and some ideas to practice and get started with the pen. There's no worries about getting burned. I tested it out, and while the plastic is a little warm when it first comes out, it's not even close to hot. This allows for a little wiggle room for moving around your design before it completely dries.

In the end, other than the sticks being a costly investment, this is a great little invention, and we've loved it so far!
text_fidelity_b: 3Doodler Start Essentials 3D Pen Set For Kids with Free Refill Filament - STEM Toy For Boys & Girls, Age 6 & Up - Toy of The Year Award Winner

text_fidelity_a:
TAG -- Live-Action Elimination Competition -- Eliminate Your Target Until You're The Last One Standing -- 4-10 Players -- Ages 14+ When I was in high school my senior class played an elimination game that was vaguely similar to this (and has been around for years and is still played across the country). Each person drew a name and that was the "target", and there were only loose rules on how to "eliminate" your target (most memorable weapon was a seltzer bottle), and graduation was the time limit. TAG is basically a formalization of that game, with fewer players and more specifics on elimination.

My graduating class had over 500 people, and not all of them played the game. Still, with 50+ players and months to play, it was unwieldy then. TAG limits the game to 10 players max, and the time frame can span anywhere from an hour or two to several weeks. Though the rules are flexible enough to allow for playing for months, this gets a bit cumbersome when having a small player pool.

Each player gets an ID card ("credentials") and a target name. Unlike the more informal version of the game, players are given specific instructions on how to eliminate their target. It might be luring the target to a location or lying in wait, getting the target to do something, or more. Nailing the target with the squirt gun or "poisoning" their food with salt might be fun but if it's not on the specific method card, it doesn't count. Once you've eliminated your target, your next target becomes whoever your original target was stalking. Gameplay continues until there's only one player left.

I like the way this game refines the elimination process, and I like the smaller, more limited scope. This makes it a good game for family events, fun in the dorms at school or even a company morale booster.

If you've ever played the old elimination game, this will be familiar territory. If you haven't it's a fun introduction. There's reasonably good replayability and there's enough flexibility to either play quickly or draw it out for days and weeks.
text_fidelity_b: TAG -- Live-Action Elimination Competition -- Eliminate Your Target Until You're The Last One Standing -- 4-10 Players -- Ages 14+

text_fidelity_a: Disney Colorbrain, The Ultimate Board Game for Families who Love Disney This game is harder than you might think. I thought my Disney knowledge was pretty good, but I was stumped on maybe 1/3 of the questions during the two games I played. My younger Disneyphiles did about the same as me. You might remember that the caterpillar in Alice in Wonderland is blue, but can you recall the color of the flags that sit atop the hats of the Tweedles? There are some questions that require you to come up with as many as five different colors, all of which must be correct for you to gain a point. What color is Celia's dress from Monsters Inc? What three colors are seen in Go Go Tomago's superhero suit from Big Hero 6?  You need to answer quickly, by putting down your selected color cards in front of you. This is actually pretty fun and interesting. Minor characters can be especially tricky. There were a few cards with answers that we disagreed with, such as the one that said Joy from Inside Out wore a yellow dress, when we all see it as green. The answer cards all have pictures from the animated films, and sometimes the photo is not great quality. My family enjoyed this game despite these issues and found it a more challenging activity than we had anticipated. It takes almost no time to learn how to set up and play. You can fill ten minutes or half an hour easily.
text_fidelity_b: Disney Colorbrain, The Ultimate Board Game for Families who Love Disney

Fisher-Price Connect Digital Soother I have to say that my baby (and my toddler) liked this soother. I, however, wouldn't say it is very soothing. It has too much stimulation going on to be considered all that soothing. (Even the 3 calmer scenes are still very active, bright, and stimulating.

This thing eats batteries. It takes about a week for it to completely deplete the batteries. Do yourself a favor and either use rechargable batteries or the lithium batteries.

I like the way this soother attaches to the crib. I've had many crib soothers and this one is the best for attachment. It has a holder that attaches easily to the crib and the soother itself pops in and out so you can move it without uninstalling it every single time. (And since it is more of a toy than a soother, you'll want to move it.)

The buttons are fairly easy to figure out, but once baby can stand or reach the thing, they can easily push the buttons themselves and cause chaos. The baby doesn't know how it works, pushes the upper buttons and makes the image on the screen change, then baby gets mad because they want their image back and they've got no clue how to do it. But you can't get them to stop pushing the buttons.

The remote only turns the thing off or on. It can't change the image or pull up one of the scenes. So, if baby hits those blasted buttons and changes the scene and gets mad about that, you can't use the remote to fix that. You can only turn the soother off or on. (And turning it on, it goes to whatever it was on when you turned it off.)

Also, if baby gets excited and hits the soother, the soother blinks out. (It turns off and turns back on.)
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Connect Digital Soother

Additionally, this kid is super into science and math since he wants to be a robotics engineer. (A decision made at the ripe old age of 6.) So, I will jump that the chance to add anything to his toy collection which will facilitate that.

Learning Resources, Geomakers, seemed like a great idea. Upon opening the package, my son immediately got to work. He started creating all kinds of shapes and things from his imagination. He made a "vision scanner," a dinosaur jaw, a tent. When you open the box there are 58 pieces total. 30 sticks in 3 different lengths, 12 curved sticks, and 16 connector spheres. The stick are all plastic and are not bendable. The spheres, which feel like rubber, have holes in them to put the sticks in. The set has a pamphlet that shows you how to make various types of objects most 3D prisms.

Cons:

It would be nice if these were laminated cards for durability.

Needs more building ideas.

The age on the box says 5+, but I would suggest this is a 4+ toy. Younger kids may not want to build what is on the pamphlet, but they can let their imagination run wild like my son, who also made a crown with this set. However, my son will be 7 soon and seems like he will age out of this quickly.

Pros:
The box that it came it was a little banged up, but otherwise it appears durable and holds all the pieces nicely. Most importantly, the stick stay inside the box and do not poke out.

I will say that my son wanted to stay up and play with this for longer and well past his bedtime. He was very interested in how many different shapes he could make.

Good for kids who hate coloring and drawing, but you want them to physically manipulate something to understand shapes.

So, three stars because the age range suggestion seems a bit high and I am uncertain of how much use my son is going to get out of this set.
text_fidelity_b: Learning Resources STEM Explorers Geomakers - 58 Pieces, Ages 5+ STEM Toys for Kids, Kindergartner Learning Toys, Shapes for Kids

I have spent the last 90 minutes trying to decorate this mug. The parts sent with the mug do not attach; you can place them but they immediately fall off. Those parts fit to one another very well, but they decline to play nicely (or at all) with their mug.

I tried LEGO pieces and they do not want to be pressed onto the mug. I really cannot blame them.

It stuck whilst still moist and them fell off when it dried and I picked up the mug to check.

We are a totally dedicated LEGO family. We have even indoctrinated...coerced...um...lovingly brought my son-in-law into the LEGO Love. We give and share those precious bricks at every gifting opportunity. There have been times when my grandchildren are out playing with their friends and my daughter and I are still inside playing. I am thinking that I will make provisions in my will for her to have one.

Makes it much easier to snap your fighter in. Also, make sure you cut off the plastic rubber band harnessed around each fighter. Otherwise they are invincible, that was a fun discovery when kiddo went undefeated and we realized it was because his guy couldn't die.

Speaking of kiddo, my son is 9 and LOVES this thing. I was bored in about 10min, but I'm guessing mid-40s mom is not the target demographic. My husband had a bit more fun, and those two really got crazy with it. There does seem to be some technique involved, past just smashing into each other until someone wins. But hey, its how I played Street Fighter back in the 80s, and mashing all the buttons is how I play Akedo in 2021.

Also, the numbers on the pieces for offense and defense are pointless. Some fighters are just better, there isn't any way around it. The defensive pieces usually just mean you will never land an attack and are pointless.

TL;DR: for the $30 the kid loves it. I could see this being a popular birthday party gift.
text_fidelity_b: Akedo Ultimate Arcade Warriors Ultimate Battle Arena Action Figure, 3 Pieces

text_fidelity_a:
Wonder Forge Richard Scarry's Busytown, Eye Found It Toddler Toy and Game (5 players) for Boys and Girls Age 3 and Up - A Fun Preschool Board Game,Multi-colored Excellent game for toddlers and preschoolers! This collaborative game (everyone works as a team) is so easy to learn and play. For two to four players, the game board is three piece, six foot long puzzle. After you set up the board, everyone has a marker. There are about ten magnifying glasses, a cardboard boat, six cardboard pieces of food, cards, a spinner, and a timer. The goal? Everyone has to make it to the boat and the boat has to make it to Picnic Island before the pigs eat all the food. The youngest person goes first.

Each player spins the spinner. The arrow lands on either a Move, a Bug, or a Pig. If you spin to a Move, you move your marker that many spaces and the next player goes. If you spin to a Pig, the Pigs "eat" one picnic food item and you take one food items away and spin again. If you spin to a bug, you pull a card. When you pull the card, you have to look throughout the game board for those items (almost Where's Waldo style). For example, if you pull a card with pictures of "balloons", you set the timer and look all around the game board for balloons. You use the magnifying glasses to mark that you've found one. When the timer is up you count how many "balloons" you found and all players move that many spaces. So if you found three balloons, everyone moves three spaces. Once everyone lands on the boat, everyone takes turns to spin to move the boat to Picnic Island. So long as the pigs haven't eaten all the food, everyone wins!

This game is a great concept for kids who have issues with winning and losing. Especially at 3 and 4 years of age when other skills like patience, taking turns, and working together are my main focus for my son rather than learning to be a gracious loser (I hope to teach him this later). Focusing and patience are the skills that this game builds as my son loves being a helper and the idea that he is helping for everyone to win actually helps him to focus and be a little more patient. The game also helps with counting and memory. I am pleasantly surprised by this game and I highly recommend it!
text_fidelity_b: Wonder Forge Richard Scarry's Busytown, Eye Found It Toddler Toy and Game (5 players) for Boys and Girls Age 3 and Up - A Fun Preschool Board Game,Multi-colored

text_fidelity_a: Chompin' Charlie Game - Feed The Squirrel Acorns And Race To Collect Them When They Scatter - Includes 24-Piece Puzzle by Goliath This is a perfect addition to the Fall basket. There are always lots of books about squirrels and acorns to add to the fall line-up and this game goes with them well. It's a great companion to those books and we've all had fun with it. There's also a little puzzle to go with the game, which adds more fun to the squirrel/acorn focus. To play the game, the players take turns rolling a die. The color/number that is rolled is what color and how many(up to 2) acorns you put into Charlie's mouth. Once he gets full, the acorns roll out the holes that are in the tree trunk that Charlie stands on. Using only one hand, the players race to collect the acorns. The first player to fill up their acorn stash card wins. The rules say that if a player rolls a certain color and it's not in the main stash of acorns, that player has to take one of their collected acorns or take one from another player. Taking from another player won't be for all families, but it can be adapted, if desired. Also, with the acorns rolling everywhere, it's tricky finding the best place to play. The acorns will roll off the table, but if on the floor, they could roll under things, like couches, if it's a smaller space. Our home is small, so we try to put up little "walls" to make sure the acorns don't roll under things. Overall, it's a fun game and the quality of it is nice, too. It's a simple game that's a great way to add a bit of joy to a day.

I’ll start with my main complaint with these first. These are dark cards, using a dark gray background for all suits, and using a dark purple for spades and clubs. This creates a low-contrast scheme that is more difficult to see in low light, and is less than pleasant even in brighter light. This is an unfortunate choice that could have been handled better. A bright purple, or even a strange color choice like orange or blue, would have worked better.

The artwork on these is impressive. A good bit of detail went into each design and it shows. The number cards (2 -10) have small designs on them that are at times hard to see and look at without a magnifying glass, though.

This are well made cards, coated and designed so they will not stick together even in damp climates. They come in a beautiful tuck box with reflective highlights in purple.

These are not bad cards at all. They’re beautiful and they’re well made, and they have some incredible artwork. However, the color scheme is not the best and these cards would be even better if the background and black suit colors were chosen a little more thoughtfully.

text_fidelity_a:
Repos JUST01 Just One, Various There are a lot of "just one word clues" games out there, from Codenames and Decrypto to games like Funglish, Crosstalk or Word Slam, and this game is yet another to add to that group. I think, however, that it's my secnd favorite of the bunch, and if you need a Codenames Killer, this might be up your alley.

In this team game, one player is attempting to guess a word that the rest of their team knows. Each team member writes down one word only, then compares to see if any matches are detected. If they are, those cards are discarded, and the guesser is left with fewer clues. Therefore, the more obtuse clues you get, the more you'll have, but it can be more difficult to deduce the word than if you're given a few obvious clues.

What I like about this game is that it manages to be a louder than usual team game with secrets. In Codenames or Crosstalk, two previous iterations of the concept, games are fun, but often it's players staring at the board in silence. In this one, you still can't say much, but it does lend itself to quicker play, and it's easier to communicate more freely once you have your clues written since your work is done, and the stress of the round is over for the clue-givers. This is a hard game, and it's definitely a word game, but lends itself to being an excellent family gathering game.
text_fidelity_b: Repos JUST01 Just One, Various

Mega Construx Pokemon Detective Pikachu Hi-hat Café Construction Set with character figures, Building Toys for Kids (328 Pieces) The Mega Construx Pokemon Detective Pikachu Hi-Hat Café set is recommended for ages 6+. I’d say the average 6-year-old will have difficulty with this set. I’m in my thirties and had trouble deciphering some of the instructions and assembling Ludicolo. And I’m used to doing UCS Lego sets!

Ludicolo is difficult to put together. When trying to fit the big beige rubbery pieces that cover the inner structure of his body, I broke off his arms several times. The rubber has to be smashed down and precisely fitted in order for the block pieces to fit and hold them in place. Then getting the lily pad head to line up properly took a few attempts, while holding the upper body piece in place.

Some of the bags of pieces are numbered and some aren’t, which I found odd. I appreciate that Mega Construx did attempt to organize them, as I’ve mentioned that in the past when assembling their sets. Having to open every bag at once and then spend time finding the pieces I need usually takes longer than the actual build.

The café is much easier to assemble, and I appreciated the cute, printed pieces, such as the cartons of milk. But beware that the pieces can take some finger strength to snap together; they definitely don’t click as easily as Lego does. Kids might have trouble with some of the steps, too; the instructions aren’t always clear.

Hot Wheels 20-Pack of 1:64 Scale Toy Sports & Race Cars, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary) It might seem as if 20 cars is too much at once. Nope! It is wonderful.

Days as a five year-old were best filled with playing in complete abandon. The freedom proffered by youth needed only a few toys to complete the ever-present joy. A few toys which mattered included several tattered but friendly books, a truck or two, an odd shovel and bucket, and, the coup de grace, a Hot Wheels car. Mattel makes a track as well, but a well-made car could take a boy places. This set of 20 is what kindergartners drool over.

A boy has everything in this set: vehicles of all colors, a few truck varieties, some funny looking cars. There are plenty, and frankly, since a few will invariably wind up lost under the couch, eaten by the dog, and buried with other treasures in the garden, having 20 quickly becomes justified.

Why a Hot Wheels car? Because they are made with hard steel. They are painted with a slick color. They hold up to frequent tastings, sand grindings, dirt smearings and other nonsense that comes with power racing in a sandbox. Sticky chocolate wipes off with warm water, and grime comes out with a good spray under the faucet.

The wheels themselves have a bounce peculiar to a genuine Hot Wheels vehicle. That's how my brother and I made sure it had adequate fuel. Ten bounces should be enough, we figured, and usually, we were right.

I fully recommend the "Hot Wheels 20-Car Gift Pack."

Anthony Trendl
AmericanSpeechwriter.com
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels 20-Pack of 1:64 Scale Toy Sports & Race Cars, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary)

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Gaming Battleship Shots We've only had this a few days so far, but my kids love it so far! They and their neighborhood friends were playing almost non-stop this entire weekend. It's a pretty unique concept and not at all what I expected coming from the original battleship: Rather than the game of strategy (and sometimes just luck!) that the traditional battleship is, this is mostly a game of skill. There is still some strategy in how you align your boats, but rather than try to determine where the other player's position is, you can see their board and have to toss one of the included ping-pong balls into the holes. Land a ball in all the boat's places, and you've sunk their ship! It is definitely reminiscent of beer pong in skillset, or perhaps one of those arcade games that require you to land a ball in a colored cup. You definitely need more space to play since there will be balls bouncing around if/when you miss, but it is a lot of fun. A creative twist on a classic game!
One thing that is a little strange to me however, is the advertising. The listing for this product says "Nostalgic tabletop gameplay meets interactive digital content for an immersive gaming experience". There's nothing digital about this, let alone interactive digital and immersive. It's a pretty fun analog pick-up-and-play game, which is what I like about it actually, but it was hard to determine what we were getting before we tried it.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Battleship Shots

Thames & Kosmos Pepper Mint in The Fantastic Underwater Science Voyage Experiment Kit I’m a big fan of the Thames & Kosmos building kits--especially the ones that teach STEM principles. However, this THAMES & KOSMOS PEPPER MINT IN THE FANTASTIC UNDERWATER SCIENCE VOYAGE EXPERIMENT KIT is definitely NOT one of my favorites. The experiments do teach about the physical properties of water (e.g., siphoning, hydraulics), but they are boring--mostly they require operating a syringe to push water through tubing.

The boat is easy to build. The parts are stamped onto thin sheets of wood. You punch the parts out of the sheets, and the edges come out smooth and clean. The parts then lock together without requiring glue or other fasteners. The assembly instructions are included in a booklet that contains a silly adventure/discovery story that features the girl character Pepper Mint.

The story is interrupted from time to time with instructions for science experiments. Each experiment has a good, easy-to-understand explanation of “what’s happening” (e.g., water can move things because, unlike air, it cannot be compressed).

The kit is apparently aimed at 11-year-old girls (Pepper Mint’s age), but the story and the experiments seem rather simplistic for that age group. I do wish that Thames & Kosmos had chosen a more serious name than “Pepper Mint” for their girl scientist. This kit has some teaching value, but it trivializes science for girls.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Pepper Mint in The Fantastic Underwater Science Voyage Experiment Kit

Elefun and Friends Barrel of Monkeys Game - Colors May Vary Ok. Here's the deal. If you actually order and receive the Elefun version produced with/through Hasbro as the current item listed as of this date shows, here's the real review by an adult:

There are 10 monkeys in a barrel. It is listed on the plastic, throw away wrapping. And that's what you get from this brand. 10. Each barrel has ten color corresponding monkeys.
About the monkeys: they are durable and not flimsy. The monkey's tails are part of the body and are not useable. All monkeys are the same mold.....BUT there are 2 each of different facial expressions. This is not so easy to notice while playing but yes, the monkeys are in facial pairs. All monkeys are the same size.

Now.....lol....from a serious player (lol) that grew up with the 60s, 70s versions: these monkeys have....two arms....one arm is bent closer to the head so it's open loop is a tad smaller. Meaning....it makes a differnece in how easy or hard it is to link them. Also....the hand shape....well....it isn't as pointed and hook like as it was years ago. So yes....it is harder and I think that's a reason there is only 10 now.

Is it fun? Yes. Worth the money?? To me....because a fast food meal costs this much. And replayablity is very high. Also....you can buy two and do color challenges. Or time two players....or lots of creativity to play.

I would rather have a reproduction of the original. BUT these are functional and in my honest review, more difficult to chain over 7; making for more competition.

I think this is a good product for children, teens, families and elderly.

**I also think this could help anyone with motor skill issues or be good for even Alzheimer persons who enjoy things simple and close up.

This is a good product.
text_fidelity_b: Elefun and Friends Barrel of Monkeys Game - Colors May Vary
